builderInsights.title: Madhu Guru
builderInsights.suggestedSummary:
Here’s one practical thing you can do this weekend to get better at building AI products.

Pick a workflow you know well - from your personal life or your work.

Automate the whole thing with AI.

Use the AI product you’re comfortable with - you’ll probably have to experiment with a few.

This exercise will force you to think about

1/ What does a great end-to-end experience look like?
2/ How should you use MCPs and tools?
3/ Where should humans stay in the loop?
4/ How do you evaluate it?

Then keep expanding the ambition.

You’ll learn more by doing this once than by reading about AI product building for a month.

The only way to learn is to build.

builderInsights.title: Guillermo Rauch
builderInsights.suggestedSummary:
これ https://t.co/ZDbjqCl3M6

Super bullish on WebMCP. Much like Tesla FSD meets the world where it is (streets, stoplights, potholes and all), agents *need* to ride the existing WWW infrastructure… WebMCP makes it more efficient.

Some pretty unique wins too. e.g: Next.js dev pages could expose debugging tools directly to agents in the specific tab they’re testing, with page-specific context, instead of sifting through server logs. No separate MCP server to find and configure because the page directly exposes its own 'agent tools'.

e.g: in this world 𝚏𝚡 + 𝚊𝚐𝚎𝚗𝚝-𝚋𝚛𝚘𝚠𝚜𝚎𝚛 is a complete web dev stack with zero loss in debugging depth

AI software factories will yield bug-free, self-improving software https://t.co/m8J9LT2wbR
